summary.headline: Havells Q2 FY27 revenue grew 35% YoY and EBITDA ~30%, but cables contribution margin fell on aluminium deflation against a high base.
summary.overview: Management said all categories grew in Q2 FY27, with revenue up 35% YoY and EBITDA up roughly 30% on operating leverage. PBT growth was moderate because the prior year included a one-time other-income gain. Cables and wires contribution margin declined YoY, while H1 cables margin was about 15%, in line with the long-term average. Lloyd grew revenue 28.5% but margins stayed subdued from raw-material inflation and off-season under-absorption. Calibrated price hikes were taken across categories, and further 5-7% hikes were flagged for Q2/Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Broadly in line with long-term average; Q2 down YoY, about 380 bps decline per analyst
YoY, volume and value both up
Down a couple of percentage points from 25%+ historical level

segments.name: Cables & Wires
segments.commentary: Cables contribution margin fell YoY on aluminium price decline against a strong base; H1 margin about 15%, guided at 15%-15.5% normal range. Overall C&W volume growth close to double digits.

segments.name: Switchgear
segments.commentary: Strong growth with volume growth close to double digits; exports about 15% of the business. Residential switchgear is largely channel-led B2C rather than order-driven.

segments.name: Lloyd (consumer durables)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 28.5% YoY with volume growth backing it; margins subdued from raw-material inflation and off-season under-absorption. RAC is about 75% of the business, with refrigerator factory commissioned in March.

segments.name: Renewables
segments.commentary: Scaling fast, sourced via Goldi Solar tie-up with no in-house manufacturing; management declined to give a peak revenue or margin target. Analyst cited roughly INR 300 crore quarterly run-rate.

guidance_outlook: No revenue guidance for FY27 given.
Management enters the festive season with a positive outlook on demand and margins, though macro uncertainty and elevated commodity prices persist.
Further price hikes of 5%-7% expected in Q2/Q3 across products, as competitors typically raise prices later.
Switchgear raw-material challenges expected to require further actions in Q3.
Lloyd margin pressure from delayed pass-through of cost increases expected to ease in Q3 and trickle into Q4 as season starts.
Capex retained at about INR 14 billion for FY27, mainly cables & wires and R&D centre.
Cables expansion on track, with full capacity on stream in about 18 months, mostly MV and EHV.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex estimate about INR 14 billion, largely cables & wires plus R&D centre.
Cables expansion on track; full expansion on stream in roughly next 18 months, mainly MV and EHV capacity.
Recent capacity expansions skewed to medium and high voltage; LV capacity considered sufficient.
Lloyd refrigerator factory fully on stream only in the last couple of months; RAC about 75% of Lloyd, target to bring to about 60% over time.
demand_pricing: Consumer demand steady despite inflationary environment; calibrated price hikes ranging 10%-25% across categories over the last 12 months, with cables and wires more than 30%.
Switchgear Q1 growth was muted by pricing actions; Q2 saw regular market demand after prices settled.
Distribution moved to pull-led from push-led (Lloyd from October, Havells from January), with 6-9 months to establish; volume growth recovering.

New entrants Crompton and Ultravolt in wires; management views Crompton as brand-led entry and others as investment-led deserving respect; sees consolidation potential in trading-led renewables players.
Lloyd market share not assessed as strong this quarter given seasonal AC trough; channel inventory normalised by end of Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Switchgear: spillover from Q1 orders, pricing contribution and margin normalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Little Q1 spillover as residential switchgear is channel-led B2C; Q2 demand regular and volume growth close to double digits. Switchgear margins recovering to 38%-39% from prior compression.

qa_highlights.question: Lloyd: volume vs price split of 28.5% growth and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth healthier than price since pricing is more muted than Havells; margin hit from under-absorption and delayed cost pass-on, expected to improve from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Wires: strategy against new entrants Crompton and Ultravolt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects organised entrants to take share from unorganised sector; will rely on product launches, distribution and influencer management, with possible margin trade-off if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Renewables: right to win, peak revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus on brand and channel via integrated system integrators, distributors and dealers; outsourced manufacturing with Goldi Solar. Declined to give a peak volume or margin target, calling it too early.

qa_highlights.question: Cables margin recovery and Lloyd profitability timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 cables margin about 15%, expected to return to normal levels; Lloyd profitability targeted in medium term but no timeline given, as guidance is avoided.

qa_highlights.question: ROCE outlook and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: ROCE currently close to 23%; management expects to improve above 23% over next couple of years, with growth and margins both expected to contribute.

risks_watch: New competitive entrants in wires could pressure pricing and shelf share in the near term.
Raw-material volatility (aluminium, copper) continues to challenge pass-through; further price hikes flagged.
Lloyd margins and under-absorption in off-season; profitability timeline not given.
Renewables margin and scale path unclear; no peak targets offered.
ROCE has fallen to about 23% from 25%+ historically while capex is elevated.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and festive-season demand, but cautious and sometimes evasive on margin trajectory, Lloyd profitability timing, and renewables targets, repeatedly declining to give specific guidance.
key_quotes: We delivered a strong performance in the second quarter, with revenue growing 35% year -on-year.
So, yes, I think wires is a very interesting category.
We're not the leading people in terms of margins in the cables business .

adds.what: Cables expansion, mainly MV and EHV capacity (full expansion)

growth.why: No revenue guidance given for FY27, though Q2 revenue grew 35% and EBITDA about 30%; further 5-7% price hikes and a cables expansion (~INR 14 bn FY27 capex, full MV/EHV capacity in ~18 months) provide partial backing.
